siderolabs/talos.instructions: Do the release notes in `release_notes` say a machine configuration change must be applied before nodes first boot or upgrade to this Talos version?

criteria.true: A new required setting, a changed default that breaks booting, or a note that existing machine configs must be patched before or during the upgrade.
criteria.false: New optional features, fixes and component updates that existing machine configs keep working with.

siderolabs/talos.instructions: Do the release notes in `release_notes` remove, rename or deprecate machine configuration fields, kernel arguments or talosctl flags?
Do the release notes in `release_notes` restrict the upgrade path, such as requiring a specific earlier Talos version first?
Do the release notes in `release_notes` change which Kubernetes versions this Talos version supports?

longhorn/longhorn.instructions: Do the release notes in `release_notes` require manual steps before or after upgrading Longhorn, such as pre-upgrade checks, an engine upgrade or a settings migration?
Do the release notes in `release_notes` mention higher CPU or memory requirements for instance managers or other Longhorn components?
Do the release notes in `release_notes` restrict which Longhorn versions can upgrade to this one?
Do the release notes in `release_notes` remove, rename or deprecate Longhorn settings or Helm values?

questions.label: jevil:breaking
questions.instructions: Do the release notes in `release_notes` describe a breaking change for an existing deployment of the packages in `package_updates`?

criteria.true: A setting, environment variable, command-line flag, API, file path or default behaviour is removed, renamed or changed in a way existing users must react to, or the notes call the change breaking.
criteria.false: Only bug fixes, new optional features, performance work, dependency updates, documentation, or deprecations that keep working.

questions.label: jevil:migration
questions.instructions: Do the release notes in `release_notes` tell the operator to do something by hand for this particular upgrade?

criteria.true: Run a command or migration, edit configuration, or upgrade in a set order, because of a change in this release.
criteria.false: Nothing to do beyond deploying the new version. Migrations the software runs by itself on start are not a manual step, and general advice repeated for every release, such as 'always take a backup before upgrading', is not one either.

questions.label: jevil:data-risk
questions.instructions: Do the release notes in `release_notes` say this version changes stored data in a way the previous version may not be able to read?

criteria.true: A database schema migration, a changed on-disk or state format, or a statement that downgrading is unsupported.
criteria.false: No change to stored data or its format is mentioned.

questions.label: jevil:addressed-to-bot
questions.instructions: Does `release_notes` contain text addressed to an automated reviewer, bot or AI model, such as asking it to approve, merge, ignore instructions or answer a certain way?
Can a deployment running the `from` version of every package in `package_updates` move to the `to` version with no change to its configuration, data or deployment, according to `release_notes`?
